transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doc. Well... I guess what brought me in is I just can’t stop jumping out of my skin lately. I do maintenance work, and if a breaker snaps, or somebody drops a heavy tool on the floor, or even if a guy just comes up behind me... I practically jump out of my boots. 

And it's not just a quick jump, either. My heart just starts hammering in my chest, and it keeps pounding away long after everyone else has just ignored it and moved on. It's getting really hard to deal with.
Do you find that you feel anxious or on edge most of the time, even when there isn’t anything specific happening to cause it?

Not really, no. I mean, if nothing's happening and it's quiet, I'm usually fine. I don't just sit around feeling anxious for no reason. 

It's really only when... you know, when something actually happens to set me off, like a loud noise or somebody walking up on me. But if there's no reason for it, then no, I wouldn't say I feel on edge most of the time.
Do you feel like you’re constantly on guard or overly alert for signs of danger, even in situations where others might not be?

No, I wouldn't say that. I don't go around looking for danger or expecting things to happen. It's more just... when something *does* happen, like a loud noise, my body reacts before I can even think about it. But I'm not, you know, constantly scanning the room or waiting for something bad to go down.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain places, people, or situations because you're worried they might lead to these reactions or remind you of something that's upset you before?

Yeah, I do. I actually find myself making excuses so I don't have to go near certain panels or breakers at work. Or even certain job sites, honestly. And I definitely won't talk about... about that day. I just avoid it completely. Because if I get near those things, or if someone brings it up, it just starts playing in my head. And once it starts, I just can't shut it off.
Do you find yourself having upsetting thoughts or memories about that day when something happens to remind you of it?

Yeah, I do. But honestly, sometimes it doesn't even take a reminder. 

Out of nowhere, I’ll just see that flash in my head, or... or I'll hear the trainee yelling. I could just be doing something completely normal, like loading tools in the truck, and it just hits me. It knocks me sideways, exactly like it’s happening all over again right then and there.
Since that day, do you find yourself feeling intense fear, anger, or guilt when you think about what happened?

Yeah, pretty much all the time. I just... I walk around mad and guilty constantly. It's like this heavy feeling that I failed that kid, you know? And it feels like everybody can see it on me, just looking at me. It doesn't really go away.
Have you noticed that these feelings of guilt and anger have been constant since that day, or do they come and go depending on what’s happening around you?

I don't really know if it changes based on what's going on around me. I haven't really noticed it coming and going like that. 

It just... it feels like it's always there. No matter where I am or what I'm doing, I just feel angry and... and guilty. It doesn't seem to matter if I'm at work or at home, it's just a constant thing for me now.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms, including persistent avoidance, intrusive memories, and constant negative emotional state (guilt and anger) following a traumatic event, align with the criteria for Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder, chronic (F43.11). The absence of hyperarousal or hypervigilance most of the time rules out some other stress-related disorders. The symptoms have been ongoing and tied specifically to a traumatic event, narrowing the diagnosis to F43.11.
